newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel weakens against dollar, basket.

text.p: The Israeli shekel weakened against the dollar and the basket of foreign currencies following the rise of the dollar abroad, dealers said.
"Trading was quiet today. In early session the shekel declined against the dollar following the dollar's rise in Europe," said a dealer at Bank Discount.
"The basket fell lower than 7.0 percent below the slope and the Bank of Israel had to intervene in the market, buying dollars to support the basket," he said.
"The shekel declined today following the rise of the dollar against the mark. The central bank intervened in the market on a relatively high scale," said another dealer.

The shekel can fluctuate in a trading band of 7.0 percent above or below a slope designed to devalue the Israeli currency at six percent a year against a basket of currencies representing Israel's main trading partners.
If the shekel-basket exchange rate reaches the lower trading band the central bank intervenes by buying foreign currency.

The representative rate for the dollar was 3.1610 against 3.1530 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, closed at 3.5451 shekels against 3.5442 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.8901 shekels per 100 yen against 2.8933 on Monday and against the mark at 2.1036 shekels per mark against 2.1135 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.1605 shekels.
